scope: Germany, France and Spain high-priority study/work pathways
policy: These records provide field-level primary-source evidence. They do not by themselves promote a pathway to publishable status; all material fields must be covered and explicitly attached to the pathway.

records.claim: Germany's Federal Foreign Office states that foreign nationals can obtain a study visa and subsequent residence permit after successful admission to a German higher-education institution.
records.methodology: Direct review of current German Federal Foreign Office study-visa guidance

records.claim: Germany requires proof that living costs for the first year of study are secured; accepted mechanisms include parental finances, a formal declaration of commitment, a German blocked account or qualifying scholarship funding.
records.methodology: Direct review of current German Federal Foreign Office financing guidance

records.claim: Germany's Opportunity Card can be accessed either by a foreign vocational or academic qualification fully recognised in Germany or through the points route requiring a qualifying foreign qualification and at least six points, alongside the applicable conditions.
records.sourceAuthority: Make it in Germany / German government
records.methodology: Direct review of current German government Opportunity Card guidance

records.claim: For 2026, Opportunity Card applicants must demonstrate sufficient funds for the job-search period; the official guidance gives a blocked-account minimum of €1,091 net per month or an applicable declaration of commitment, with qualifying part-time employment potentially counting toward the financing test.
records.sourceAuthority: Make it in Germany / German government
records.methodology: Direct review of current German government Opportunity Card financing guidance

records.claim: France-Visas states that student applicants must have selected their course or studies and be accepted by a higher-education establishment; studies longer than three months use the long-stay student route subject to the applicable formalities.
records.methodology: Direct review of current France-Visas student guidance

records.claim: France-Visas states that student long-stay visa applications submitted from 1 August 2026 require proof of resources corresponding to at least €877.50 per month.
records.methodology: Direct review of current France-Visas student campaign notice

records.claim: France-Visas describes multiple Talent Passport categories; for the highly qualified employee route, the applicant needs an employment contract of at least one year plus a recognised higher-education qualification of at least three years or comparable professional experience, subject to the category's conditions.
records.methodology: Direct review of current France-Visas international-talent guidance

records.claim: For the highly qualified employee Talent Passport category, France-Visas specifies a salary threshold tied to the annually fixed gross reference salary; the current page states €59,373 as the reference salary from 21 August 2025 and requires at least 1.5 times that reference salary for the EU Blue Card subcategory.
records.methodology: Direct review of current France-Visas international-talent salary guidance

records.claim: Spain's Ministry of Inclusion states that the long-term study stay authorisation covers recognised higher education and other qualifying full-time studies; higher-education applicants must be admitted to a recognised institution and have paid the applicable enrolment or registration fees.
records.sourceAuthority: Spanish Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration
records.methodology: Direct review of current Spanish government study-stay guidance

records.claim: Spain's study-stay guidance requires sufficient economic means for the stay and return; for the applicant's maintenance it specifies 100% of IPREM per month, with different percentages for qualifying accompanying family members and an exception where accommodation has been prepaid for the full stay.
records.sourceAuthority: Spanish Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration
records.methodology: Direct review of current Spanish government financial-means guidance

records.claim: Spain's UGE defines international teleworkers as third-country nationals carrying out remote work or professional activity for companies located outside Spain using computer, telematic and telecommunications systems; professional applicants may have Spanish business relationships provided the applicable 20% activity limit is respected.
records.sourceAuthority: Spanish Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration / UGE
records.methodology: Direct review of current Spanish UGE teleworker guidance and FAQ

records.claim: Spain's official international-teleworker FAQ states that applicants must prove sufficient employment-derived resources, with the holder requirement set at 200% of the minimum interprofessional salary per month and additional percentages for accompanying family members.
records.sourceAuthority: Spanish Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration / UGE
records.methodology: Direct review of current Spanish UGE international-teleworker FAQ
